title: Beacon-confirmed human clicks are rare in direct landing mode
class_symptom: A confirmation that depends on client-side JavaScript running on a page covers almost no real visitors when the flow redirects before any page renders.
mechanism: With landing_mode=direct, real visitors are 302-redirected straight to the partner and never load the page that runs the JS confirmation beacon, so is_confirmed_human is set for very few real clicks.

evidence: Referral non-bot clicks: 24 of 251 confirmed human.
Partner-direct non-bot clicks: 1 of 422 confirmed human.

measurements: Count of is_confirmed_human clicks among non-bot clicks, per link type, measured 2026-11-04: referral 24/251, partner-direct 1/422.
Consequence: using confirmed-human as the headline human count in direct mode would show about 25 instead of about 673.

detection.reason: Documented limit of the design, not a defect a check can catch; any report that headlines confirmed-human clicks in direct mode must say so.
